faqs.a: PAN follows the format AAAAA9999A: five letters, four digits, one letter. The 4th letter tells the holder type - P for individual person, C for company, H for HUF, and so on. The 5th letter is usually the first letter of the holder's surname or name.
faqs.q: What is the format of a PAN card number?

faqs.a: The 4th character: P = Person (individual), C = Company, H = HUF (Hindu Undivided Family), F = Firm, A = Association of Persons, T = Trust, B = Body of Individuals, L = Local Authority, J = Artificial Juridical Person, G = Government.
faqs.q: What does the 4th letter of PAN mean?

faqs.a: No. Structural validation only confirms the number looks right. The income tax department's database is the only authority that can confirm a PAN is real and active.
faqs.q: Does a valid format mean the PAN is genuine?

faqs.a: It is usually fine for drafts and learning. For anything official - KYC, bank accounts, tax filings - always copy it from the actual PAN card. One wrong letter can route your money or records to the wrong person.
faqs.q: Can I use a sample PAN on official forms?

faqs.a: Yes. PAN is uppercase by design, and this validator converts your input automatically. Lowercase, extra spaces, and mixed case are all accepted and normalized.

First, check for typos - a single wrong character is the most common cause. If it still fails, the number may be incomplete or fictitious. Never alter a PAN to force it to validate; get the correct number from the card.

pan-validator.formula:
PAN structure: AAAAA9999A
Positions 1-3: alphabetic serial (AAA to ZZZ)
Position 4: holder type code (C, P, H, F, A, T, B, L, J, G)
Position 5: first letter of surname / entity name
Positions 6-9: numeric serial (0001 to 9999)
Position 10: alphabetic check character (A to Z)
howTo: Type or paste the 10-character PAN into the input box.
The validator checks it live: length, pattern, and holder-type code.
A green message means the format is valid; a red message explains exactly what is wrong.
Read the breakdown to see what each position of the PAN represents.
keyFacts: A PAN is exactly 10 characters: 5 letters, 4 digits, 1 letter.
The 4th character encodes the holder type: P for person, C for company, H for HUF, and 7 more codes.
The 5th character is usually the first letter of the holder's surname or entity name.
Positions 6-9 are a running number from 0001 to 9999.
The last character is an alphabetic check character.
Structure alone never proves a PAN is issued or active - only the tax database can do that.
